cards.text: Solomon, king of Israel and son of David, is about to build the house of the LORD. This is the BIG one, friend. The Bible dates this moment by counting all the way back to when Israel came out of Egypt.

cards.question: Solomon begins building the house of the LORD in the ___ year after the Israelites came out of Egypt.
Solomon starts building the house of the LORD in his very first year as king.

cards.text: Up it goes: a house sixty cubits long, twenty wide and thirty high, with a porch out front, narrow windows up high, and three floors of side rooms around it, all roofed with cedar. The stones were cut at the quarry, so no hammer, no chisel, no iron tool was heard at the temple while it was being built. A construction site with NO noise? Friend, I've heard one man hang ONE shelf and it sounded like a drum solo.
Then the word of the LORD comes to Solomon about this temple he's building. And God doesn't mention one beam. Not one plank. Not ONE cubit.

cards.question: God says He'll fulfill through Solomon the promise He made to David, but there's an 'if.' What does Solomon need to do?

answers.text: Walk in God's statutes and keep His commandments
Bring a thousand offerings to the new altar
Build the temple bigger than any palace

cards.question: God's promise to David will come through Solomon no matter how Solomon lives.
Then God says what He'll do for His people: He will ___ among the Israelites and will not abandon His people Israel.

cards.text: So Solomon builds the temple and finishes it, and the inside is something else. Cedar walls carved with gourds, palm trees, open flowers and cherubim, and at the back, the Most Holy Place, prepared for the ark of the covenant of the LORD, with two olive wood cherubim whose wings stretch wall to wall and touch in the middle. Then GOLD: over the whole interior, the floor, the altar, the doors and the cherubim. I spent years in a drawer under a takeout menu, and this man's walls are GOLD.
The foundation went down in the fourth year of Solomon's reign. The finish comes in the eleventh year, in the month of Bul.

cards.question: When Solomon is done in the eleventh year, a few parts of the temple are still left unfinished.
From the foundation in Solomon's fourth year to the finish in his eleventh, how long did building the temple take?

cards.text: That's where we'll leave it for now. Keep that apron on, friend, because this story isn't over.

findings.problem: The setup says God 'doesn't mention one beam. Not one plank. Not ONE cubit.' That tells the baker the condition has nothing to do with building, which rules out the wrong answer 'Build the temple bigger than any palace' on card 6.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card cites 1 Kings 6:14-36, but it never uses verse 36 (the inner courtyard of dressed stone and cedar beams). The citation is wider than what the card tells. Either cite 6:14-35 or add the courtyard to the summary.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Card 9 already says 'So Solomon builds the temple and finishes it,' and card 10 says 'The finish comes in the eleventh year.' The question itself also opens with 'When Solomon is done.' All of these give away the answer (False) to whether parts are still unfinished.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The 'story isn't over' line copies the doc's example almost word for word ('That's where we'll leave it for now...'). It should be written fresh.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
